question: Raja Parba festival of Odisha is the living cultural heritage and agricultural way of life. It is held for three days in the month of ______.
solution:
The correct answer is June.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raja Parba** is a festival celebrated in the state of Odisha, India.
 
• The festival is held for three days and marks the onset of the agricultural season.
 
• Raja Parba is celebrated in the month of June, which is also the month of the first rainfall in the state.
 
• The festival is celebrated to honor Mother Earth and the fertility of the soil.
 
• During the festival, women are given a break from household chores, and the men engage in games and sports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Odisha is the eleventh most populous state in terms of population and the eighth largest in terms of land.
 
• The third-largest Scheduled Tribe population in India is found in this state.
 
• It shares borders with Andhra Pradesh to the south, Chhattisgarh to the west, and the states of Jharkhand and West Bengal to the north.
 
• Along the Indian Ocean's Bay of Bengal, Odisha boasts a 485-kilometer (301-mile) coastline.
 
• An additional name for the area is Utkala, and the national hymn of India, "Jana Gana Mana," refers to it by this name.
 
• Odia is the language spoken in Odisha and is one of India's classical languages.
